text:
For most households preparing for a **multi-day hurricane outage**, I’d choose the **[BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 + 200 W solar-panel kit](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2-200w-solar-kit)**. It has a 2,073.6 Wh battery, and the comparison says it can keep a fridge and CPAP going through a day and night; its 1,000 W solar input also gives you room to add panels later. The listed price was **$1,199** when checked, but confirm the current price and stock. ([Dealectric’s hurricane-kit comparison](https://dealectric.com/best-solar-generator-kit-for-hurricane-season))

If you mainly need backup for smaller essentials and want to spend less, the same comparison lists the **[BLUETTI AC180 + 200 W kit](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180-200w-solar-kit)** at $729.

Either way, treat solar as a way to recharge between sunny periods—not a guarantee during days of heavy cloud or rain—and check that the station’s output can handle the appliances you plan to plug in.
